DECISION (2026-11-28, Mark): option 1 — follow upstream and do not pretend otherwise. 'at this time we are not going to pretend they are ready, whenever they make 0.x.y api change, we will just eat it and follow.'

So: no insulation layer, no artificial 1.0 gate, no abstraction over the formats crates. RustCrypto's pre-1.0 churn is absorbed as it arrives, and PKIX stays pre-1.0 while its public API carries pre-1.0 types. A der or x509-cert minor bump is a breaking PKIX release, and that is the honest reporting of what actually broke rather than something to be hidden.

Rejects option 2 (own certificate handle at the boundary) — it is a large piece of work that argues against the crate's premise of being thin over the formats layer, and it would make every caller holding an x509_cert::Certificate convert.

Rejects option 4 (ship 1.0 anyway) — that is the pretence this decision is against.

Option 3 (re-export x509_cert and der so consumers can name one version) is not settled by this and is not blocking. It is a convenience, not a stability claim, and could be taken later without reopening this decision. Noting it here rather than filing a separate bead, since it is a few lines whenever someone wants it.

Do not reopen at each dependency bump — that is what this bead was for. The levels as measured: signature 3.0.0 and ed25519-dalek 3.0.0 are post-1.0; der 0.8.3, spki 0.8.1, x509-cert 0.3.1, rsa 0.10.0, p256/p384/p521 0.14.0, sha2/sha1 0.11.1, digest 0.11.3 and elliptic-curve 0.14.3 are not, and the formats layer is the one in the public API.
